maze package

Submodules

maze.cellular_automata module

Cellular Automata based maze and cave generator.

Generates organic, cave-like environments with natural obstacle clusters using 2D cellular automata without artificial perimeter wall enclosures.

maze.cellular_automata.count_wall_neighbors_inbounds(grid: List[List[int]], r: int, c: int, wall_value: int = 1) → int

Count obstacle neighbors in the 8-Moore neighborhood within grid boundaries.

Only in-bounds neighbors are counted to prevent artificial border clustering.

Parameters:

  • grid (List[List[int]]) – 2D grid matrix.

  • r (int) – Row coordinate.

  • c (int) – Column coordinate.

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Cell value for obstacles. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

Number of neighboring wall cells.

Return type:

int

maze.cellular_automata.generate_ca_maze(height: int, width: int, seed: int | None = None, initial_wall_prob: float = 0.42, iterations: int = 2, survive_thresh: int = 3, birth_thresh: int = 5, wall_value: int = 1, path_value: int = 0, fill_small_components: bool = True) → List[List[int]]

Generate an organic cave/maze with obstacle clusters using Cellular Automata.

Initializes random noise across the full grid without forced border walls, then applies birth/survival cellular automata rules iteratively to generate natural organic obstacle clusters and corridors. Disconnected open pockets are filled into obstacles to guarantee a unified navigable open space.

Parameters:

  • height (int) – Grid height (number of rows).

  • width (int) – Grid width (number of columns).

  • seed (Optional[int], optional) – Random seed. Defaults to None.

  • initial_wall_prob (float, optional) – Initial random obstacle density. Defaults to 0.42.

  • iterations (int, optional) – Smoothing iterations. Defaults to 2.

  • survive_thresh (int, optional) – Min wall neighbors for wall survival. Defaults to 3.

  • birth_thresh (int, optional) – Min wall neighbors to create wall from path. Defaults to 5.

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Value representing obstacle. Defaults to 1.

  • path_value (int, optional) – Value representing free path. Defaults to 0.

  • fill_small_components (bool, optional) – Whether to fill isolated open pockets. Defaults to True.

Returns:

2D grid matrix of the generated maze.

Return type:

List[List[int]]

Raises:

ValueError – If dimensions < 3 or probability outside [0, 1].

maze.kruskal module

Randomized Kruskal’s Algorithm for maze generation.

This module generates perfect mazes (spanning trees) or braided mazes using Randomized Kruskal’s algorithm with Disjoint Set Union (DSU) and seed reproducibility.

class maze.kruskal.DisjointSetUnion

Bases: object

Disjoint Set Union (DSU) / Union-Find data structure with path compression.

Union the sets containing items a and b.

Parameters:

  • b (Tuple[int, int]) – Second item.

Returns:

True if sets were merged, False if already in the same set.

bool

maze.kruskal.generate_kruskal_maze(height: int, width: int, seed: int | None = None, braid_ratio: float = 0.0, wall_value: int = 1, path_value: int = 0) → List[List[int]]

Generate a maze using Randomized Kruskal’s algorithm.

Creates a 2D grid filled with walls and carves passages connecting rooms in a spanning tree topology. Optional braiding can remove dead ends to create multiple alternative paths.

Parameters:

  • height (int) – Grid height (number of rows). Must be >= 3.

  • width (int) – Grid width (number of columns). Must be >= 3.

  • seed (Optional[int], optional) – Random seed for reproducibility. Defaults to None.

  • braid_ratio (float, optional) – Ratio (0.0 to 1.0) of extra openings to carve to remove dead-ends and introduce loops. Defaults to 0.0.

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Cell value representing walls. Defaults to 1.

  • path_value (int, optional) – Cell value representing open paths. Defaults to 0.

Returns:

2D grid matrix where 0 represents path and 1 represents wall.

Return type:

List[List[int]]

Raises:

ValueError – If height < 3 or width < 3.

maze.validation module

Maze validation and geometric analysis utilities.

This module provides functions for path verification, geodesic distance calculation, connected components extraction, and Bresenham’s line-of-sight determination.

maze.validation.bfs_shortest_distances(start: Tuple[int, int], valid_cells: Set[Tuple[int, int]]) → Tuple[Dict[Tuple[int, int], int], Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]]

Compute shortest distances and predecessors from start cell to all reachable cells.

Parameters:

  • start (Tuple[int, int]) – Origin cell (row, col).

  • valid_cells (Set[Tuple[int, int]]) – Set of traversable cells.

Returns:

A tuple of (distances_dict, predecessors_dict).

Return type:

Tuple[Dict[Tuple[int, int], int], Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]]

maze.validation.bresenham_line(start: Tuple[int, int], end: Tuple[int, int]) → List[Tuple[int, int]]

Generate grid coordinates along a line using Bresenham’s algorithm.

Parameters:

  • start (Tuple[int, int]) – Starting coordinates (row, col).

  • end (Tuple[int, int]) – Ending coordinates (row, col).

Returns:

Ordered list of integer coordinates forming the line.

Return type:

List[Tuple[int, int]]

Example

>>> bresenham_line((0, 0), (2, 2))
[(0, 0), (1, 1), (2, 2)]
maze.validation.compute_maximum_geodesic_distance(grid: List[List[int]], wall_value: int = 1) → Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int], int, List[Tuple[int, int]]]

Find the pair of open cells with the maximum geodesic distance.

Searches within the largest connected component of traversable cells using all-pairs shortest paths via BFS. This guarantees start and goal are as far apart as possible along the maze paths and that a valid path exists.

Parameters:

  • grid (List[List[int]]) – 2D grid where wall_value represents obstacles.

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Obstacle cell value. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

(start_coord, goal_coord, max_geodesic_distance, shortest_path).

Return type:

Tuple[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int], int, List[Tuple[int, int]]]

Raises:

ValueError – If no open connected component with at least 2 cells is found.

maze.validation.find_connected_components(grid: List[List[int]], wall_value: int = 1) → List[Set[Tuple[int, int]]]

Identify all 4-connected components of open cells in the grid.

Parameters:

  • grid (List[List[int]]) – 2D grid matrix.

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Obstacle identifier value. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

List of connected component sets sorted by size descending.

Return type:

List[Set[Tuple[int, int]]]

maze.validation.get_open_cells(grid: List[List[int]], wall_value: int = 1) → Set[Tuple[int, int]]

Retrieve all open (non-wall) coordinates from the grid.

Parameters:

  • grid (List[List[int]]) – 2D grid matrix.

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Value representing obstacle/wall. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

Set of (row, col) tuples corresponding to open cells.

Return type:

Set[Tuple[int, int]]

maze.validation.has_line_of_sight(grid: List[List[int]], start: Tuple[int, int], end: Tuple[int, int], wall_value: int = 1) → bool

Check if there is an unblocked line of sight between two grid positions.

Uses Bresenham’s line algorithm to trace points between start and end. Intermediate wall cells block the line of sight.

Parameters:

  • grid (List[List[int]]) – 2D grid matrix where wall_value represents obstacles.

  • start (Tuple[int, int]) – Origin coordinates (row, col).

  • end (Tuple[int, int]) – Target coordinates (row, col).

  • wall_value (int, optional) – Integer representing a wall obstacle. Defaults to 1.

Returns:

True if there is a clear line of sight, False if blocked by a wall.

Return type:

bool

maze.validation.reconstruct_path(start: Tuple[int, int], goal: Tuple[int, int], predecessors: Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]) → List[Tuple[int, int]]

Reconstruct coordinate path from start to goal using predecessor map.

Parameters:

  • start (Tuple[int, int]) – Origin coordinate.

  • goal (Tuple[int, int]) – Goal coordinate.

  • predecessors (Dict[Tuple[int, int], Tuple[int, int]]) – Predecessor mapping from BFS.

Returns:

Complete path from start to goal inclusive.

Return type:

List[Tuple[int, int]]

Module contents

Maze generation and validation package.

Provides algorithms for maze synthesis (Randomized Kruskal, Cellular Automata) and geometric validation (geodesic distance, connectivity, Bresenham line of sight).
